aria: Animated recap of the Nets' 104 to 97 win at Milwaukee: Noah Clowney's 26-foot 3-pointer with 6:38 left that made it 88 to 78, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Julius Randle's 28 points, the top scorers, how the Nets won, and the next game.

notes: Box score from StatMuse's game page for the Nets' 104–97 win at Milwaukee on Nov 25, 2026: all 104 Brooklyn points and all 97 Milwaukee points add up from the player lines, as do the shooting totals (37 of 89, 10 of 38 from three, 20 of 26 FT for Brooklyn; 38 of 89, 11 of 44, 10 of 16 for Milwaukee), rebounds (52–44), assists (23–26) and steals (10–7). The quarter scores (28–23–26–27 to 24–23–24–26) are on StatMuse; 51–47 at the half is also in Field Level Media, the NY Post and SB Nation, and 77–71 after three in the NY Post, Roundtable Sports and SB Nation. Biggest leads (Brooklyn 14, Milwaukee 7) are on StatMuse and HoopsNightly. Bench points: Brooklyn 42 (NY Daily News; StatMuse box), Milwaukee 30 (StatMuse box). Brooklyn's 24 points off turnovers are in the NY Daily News and Nets Wire. Records are from the game stories (Nets 4–13, Bucks 2–17; NY Daily News, NY Post); ranks are from the site's standings after Wednesday's games.

The win snapped Brooklyn's five-game losing streak (AP; Field Level Media; NY Post) and was the Nets' first NBA Cup win; they are 1–2 in group play and Milwaukee 0–3 (AP; Field Level Media). Day'Ron Sharpe's cutting dunk off Egor Dëmin's pass with 3:43 left in the third made it 68–67, the last lead change (StatMuse; NY Daily News; Fastbreak Journal). Randle had 16 first-half points (AP; NY Post); Clowney scored a season-high 17 (Roundtable Sports), 9 of them in the fourth (NY Daily News; Nets Wire); Sharpe had a season-high 14 rebounds (NY Daily News). Moritz Wagner left with left knee soreness and did not return after halftime (AP; NY Post). Next: Brooklyn visits Toronto on Friday in the NBA Cup (AP; Roundtable Sports; CBS Sports schedule); Milwaukee visits Detroit on Friday (AP; CBS Sports schedule).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Noah Clowney's 3-pointer with 6:38 left that made it 88–78: StatMuse's scoring plays have "N. Clowney makes 26' three Assisted by J. Randle" at 6:38 of the fourth for 85–78 to 88–78; Fastbreak Journal also has the 26-foot 3-pointer for 88–78 at 6:38, and Roundtable Sports has Clowney's dunk and a three making it 88–78. So the board's Nets +7 to +10 is 85–78 to 88–78. The defender and the spot on the floor aren't described, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from beyond the arc. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Brooklyn Nets or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Clowney's listed 6-foot-10 and 210 pounds (RealGM), with arms at the default length because no wingspan is reported there, in the Nets' road kit with No. 21 (RealGM) and the default darker skin tone, since he has no approved look yet. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
